pairs.difference: A: cyan ring background sits inside the real range. The red backboard frame and orange rim stand against a near-white panel that rests the eye, though the white inflates the shadow ratio (2.46). B: hot magenta background (0.234) is above the real range and is louder than the hero. In the lens the orange beads dissolve into the pink, and the steel rings turn blue, so the card reduces to 1.7 hue families, below real. Pure pink against pure blue.
pairs.fix: Lower the pink background to a dusty rose with less saturation than the blue sphere. Keep the rings neutral grey steel with a warm and a cool side. Keep the orange beads clearly orange against the pink.

pairs.difference: A: cyan fan with crimson box, tan lining and gold medal. Box shadows go to rich wine, and the tan lining gives neutral rest; the 5.4 hue families is slightly high. B: violet fan (0.275) is far above real and overpowers the subject (0.085). In the lens the straps, red caps and flames merge into one mauve, and the tanks into beige, so only 2 families remain.
pairs.fix: Make the purple background deeper and less saturated. Keep the straps dark brown, the caps true red and the flame yellow as separate colors, and let the steel tanks reflect a little of the purple only at the edges.

pairs.difference: A: blue sky, blue trim, blue door and blue window on peach-cream walls. It is nearly one hue plus cream, with low warm share (0.087), and shaded areas are more colorful than lit ones (1.49, just above real). This is the cream-white seen on generated lesson cards. B: night navy with pink, amber and green signs and brown wood. All fields are in range and its five hue families have clear roles.
pairs.fix: Paint the walls a neutral off-white, not peach, with cool grey-blue shadows. Reduce the blue repeats: door and trim in a different muted color, one small warm accent.

pairs.difference: A: pure blue bottle on a yellow-orange fan, one flat blue mass in the lens, warm share slightly high (0.78). B: blue pool with lilac-white goal and one orange ball accent, warm share slightly low (0.04), shadow ratio slightly high (1.56). Each misses the real range narrowly and in opposite directions, and both hue setups match the real cards. Color gives no reason to choose.

A: magenta wall and pink floor with rainbow flowers. The tan stones are a neutral rest, and all fields are in range, although the flowers are very pure. B: dull mauve wall and bench behind the books. Background chroma (0.071) is half the real minimum and hue count (9.6) is about double the real maximum. Saturated blue, crimson and green books sit in a muddy room with no single background color.
pairs.fix: Replace the grey-mauve room with one clean, moderately saturated background color. Limit the scene to three book colors plus cream pages, and keep the window and drawer colors quiet.

pairs.difference: A: butter-cream cabinet on a pale pastel blue room (background 0.086, below real). The cream runs across the whole lit body, the same warm ivory cast as the generated computers in the lessons, and the only chroma is small red LEDs. B: this is the real computer from the lessons, with cool grey-white plastic, a blue-grey side plane and a strong orange background. Low subject chroma on both cards does not separate them, because the real one is also low.
pairs.fix: Make the cabinet a neutral light grey-white, not cream, with a blue-grey side. Use a stronger, more saturated blue background so the pale object separates by color.

pairs.difference: A: green body and blue lenses on orange wood, a clear contrast between hero and floor. Shadows on the wood stay brown-olive and related to the floor; warm share and hue count are in range. B: yellow arm on green is an adjacent-hue pair, with warm share (0.22) and hue count (2.4) below real. The tile floor and cast shadow go colorless grey (0.21 shadow ratio) and the yellow falls to pale cream in the lens.
pairs.fix: Give the shadow on the floor a color: cool blue-green tinted, not grey. Tint the floor toward the background, and add a contrasting accent color to the arm instead of yellow on green.

pairs.difference: A: teal car with silver trim and pale seats on warm yellow. Teal against yellow is close to real hue roles, and the silver supplies neutrals, though warm share is high (0.81). B: scarf is near-pure red, with subject chroma 0.217 above the real maximum. The red stays pure into the folds, so there is almost no neutral on the subject, like the overpushed objects on the generated lesson cards. Weak call, because A is also out of range on warmth.
pairs.fix: Make the red cloth a slightly deeper, less pure red with folds shifting to dark wine. Add a soft neutral sheen on the raised folds.

pairs.difference: A: hot magenta tray, cyan ice and orange wood, three loud hues with 6 families, slightly above real, but the hues hold distinct roles and the frost adds neutral. B: mint phone, orange handset and violet background with lilac-white floor. Warm share (0.11) and hue count (2.8) are slightly low, but the floor gives a clear rest. Both misses are small and in opposite directions.

A: blue plane in blue sky with white clouds, one hue family in practice. Warm share is 0, subject and background chroma are both below real, and the shadow ratio (2.24) is far above real because only the shaded belly carries color. There is no warm accent anywhere. B: gold body, red dish and navy panels on cyan, with all fields in range and clear hero, background and accent roles.
pairs.fix: Add one warm accent such as a red or orange tail stripe. Raise the sky to a richer blue, and give the white fuselage warm light with grey-blue shadows rather than pure saturated blue under the body.

pairs.difference: A: blue shoes carry lime, teal, magenta and orange details on orange and cream. The accents are scattered and 5.5 hue families is above real, with the soles turning lilac over the yellow floor. B: pure green liquid against orange, a single hero hue with cork as the small accent and a pale neutral shelf for rest; it stays in range except a slightly low background.
pairs.fix: Limit the shoes to blue plus one accent color. Remove the extra pink, orange and teal details from the laces and soles.

pairs.difference: A: teal wall, teal floor and teal-tinted metal, with pink glow as the only other color. Warm share (0.02) is below real, hue count (3.1) just below, and the steel reads blue in the lens with almost no neutral. B: orange wood and red ring on cyan water with a sand corner, a strong warm/cool split and 6.3 families in range. Its low shadow ratio (0.54) comes from dark charcoal posts under the pier, a small mass.
pairs.fix: Keep the steel cap and base a neutral grey with a warm highlight. Shift the room to a deeper, darker color so it differs from the metal, and add one small warm light in the base.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away through pushed hue and weak neutrals. In the lessons they differ from the real cards in four ways: backgrounds run brighter and cleaner (more cyan, hotter orange); objects are pushed toward pure hue (orange glove, cobalt camera); whites drift to butter-cream instead of cool grey-white with blue-grey side planes; and metal or white parts lose their own neutral color to the card's main hue. In the test pairs the same faults appear as a single hue spread across hero and background, with metal and white taking on that hue, or a background louder than the hero. Hue-family counts outside the real range are the second tell: about 2 or fewer on loud one-hue cards, above 5 on scattered rainbow detail.
